projection.growthBasis: Annual figure used as a constant rate; not projected. WHO 2022 estimate: USD 1.7 trillion per year in healthcare costs and lost productivity, equivalent to 1.7% of global GDP.

source: WHO — Economic cost of tobacco use, 2022 update

sources.name: American Cancer Society — Cancer Treatment & Survivorship Facts and Figures

categories.methodology: Approximate full-course cost of treating one patient with non-small-cell lung cancer in a high-income setting (surgery + platinum-based chemotherapy + immunotherapy + radiotherapy + follow-up), drawn from ACS cost-of-care estimates.

sources.name: USPSTF — Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Recommendation Statement

categories.methodology: Per-quitter cost of an evidence-based cessation program: nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) plus brief behavioural counselling, US public-health pricing.

sources.name: WHO — MPOWER Tobacco Control Investment Cases
WHO FCTC — The Global Case for Investment in Tobacco Control

categories.methodology: Average annual cost for a single low- or middle-income country to fully implement the WHO MPOWER package (tax, smoke-free policies, cessation services, packaging, advertising bans, monitoring) at scale, from WHO investment-case median.

sources.name: Stop TB Partnership — Global Plan to End TB

categories.methodology: Per-patient cost of a full DOTS course of TB treatment in low- and middle-income settings (drugs + diagnosis + supervised delivery), from WHO Global TB Report median.

sources.name: GOLD — Global Strategy for the Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of COPD

categories.methodology: Annual cost of evidence-based COPD care for one moderate-severity patient (inhaled therapy + exacerbation management + pulmonary rehab) in an upper-middle-income setting, from GOLD report ranges.

sources.name: Sriudomporn, Watts, Sim et al. — Achieving Immunization Agenda 2030 coverage targets for 14 pathogens: Projected product and immunization delivery costs for 194 Countries, 2021–2030 (Vaccine: X 2022)
Gavi, The Vaccine Alliance — Resource Mobilisation Process

categories.methodology: Estimated ~USD 27 billion/year to deliver a full routine immunisation schedule to every child globally, per the IA2030 costing (Sriudomporn, Watts, Sim et al., Vaccine: X 2022).

sources.name: Laborde et al. — Ending hunger: science must stop neglecting smallholder farmers, Nature 2020

categories.methodology: Average additional annual public expenditure (~USD 33 billion) required from donors and low/middle-income governments through 2030 to end hunger (SDG 2), per IFPRI models published in Nature Food.

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene

categories.methodology: Annual capital investment of ~USD 37.6 billion needed through 2030 for universal safely-managed drinking water (SDG 6.1 component), per the World Bank's SDG 6 costing study (Hutton & Varughese 2016).
